criteria.evidence: Read from the diff: athena.toml has only added lines, at lines 81–101. No existing line was changed or removed.

criteria.criterion: The test in crates/athena-cap-study/src/lib.rs no longer asserts the section is absent; it asserts capability("study") is present and that the producer/verifier commands and checks come from it, and the test name no longer says 'nothing_is_configured_yet'.
criteria.evidence: Read from the diff: the test is renamed to the_verifier_never_writes_and_grants_and_checks_come_from_the_config. It calls `jc.config.capability(ID).expect(...)`. It asserts that the producer and verifier grant commands equal the section's commands and are not empty, that the check names are [fmt, clippy, test], and that env equals section.env. job_config() reads the real athena.toml through include_str!, so the test fails if the section is removed.

criteria.criterion: athena.toml is listed as a deliverable and named here as a governance file changed; no firstmate pinning is added.
criteria.evidence: Read from the brief and the diff: athena.toml is an expected deliverable marked as a governance file. The new CHANGELOG entry says "This is a governance file change; the section governs later jobs only." The diff adds no firstmate pinning.

summary: The change passes and does what the retry asked. It adds a `[capabilities.study]` section to athena.toml, with its environment table and three checks (fmt, clippy, test). The section is an exact copy of the `[capabilities.change]` section, no existing table changed, and nothing pins firstmate. The study crate test no longer checks that the section is missing. It now loads the real athena.toml and checks that the section exists and that the study capability's commands, checks and environment come from it, so removing the section would make it fail. CHANGELOG.md records the addition and says it changes a governance file. I ran `cargo test --locked` (all suites passed, including the study crate's 28 tests and the tests that parse athena.toml), `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` (no warnings) and `cargo fmt --all --check` (no differences).
